transcript:
[00:00] Liam: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Liam, AE on Redwood. Priya's our solutions engineer. Today we'll walk the Optimize console and talk through batching + cache recs for your chat/search workload.
[00:18] Samantha: Hi ya, thanks. we want to see concretely where we can get cost down without breaking the 120ms p50 latency target. we also have compliance constraints — logs need to stay in our VPC.
[00:31] Liam: Great. we'll cover hosted + private choices but focus on the Optimize runbook so you can get savings on hosted first. Priya, can you share the console?
[00:42] Priya: Yep sharing now. you might see my screen flicker — sorry. Loading Optimize > Profiles. We have pre-built presets: low-latency, throughput, and cost-optimized. For Eden's mix (short prompts + long context retrieval) we'd likely start with "hybrid-prefetch" preset.
[01:05] Diego: what's hybrid-prefetch? is that the same as sessionization?
[01:10] Priya: It's a mix — session affinity for recurrent users plus lookahead prefix cache for retrieved contexts so KV hits on subsequent tokens. basically we cache the KV for the model's context window for repeated prefixes. the terminology in our docs is sometimes "prefix cache" or "KV lookahead".
[01:30] Nora: quick clarification — is the KV stored in Redwood's managed cache or in our VPC for private?
[01:36] Liam: For hosted, the cache is managed by Redwood but we offer an optional VPC-backed cache for Private deployments. for pilot we'll use managed cache but can switch to VPC for production to meet your data residency.
[01:48] Samantha: ok sounds good. show us numbers.
[01:52] Priya: switching to the savings simulator in Console. I loaded a sample workload with your session length distribution (we used the anonymized trace you sent last month). Here's baseline: p50 95ms, p95 310ms, token cost X. If we enable prefix KV with a 12h TTL and 70% hit-rate assumption, token cost drops ~42% in the sim but p95 goes up ~20ms due to cache lookup.
[02:20] Diego: 70% hit-rate — where did that come from? our retrievals vary.
[02:24] Priya: right, it's an assumption based on 1) your repeated prompts per session 2) how often the retriever returns the same top-3 docs. we can parameterize that. in the spreadsheet (cost_model_v3.xlsx) we have columns for hit_rate, avg_prefix_len, and average tokens_per_response.
[02:41] Samantha: can you show the tradeoff with batching? we batch at the client now but only tiny batches of 2-3 reqs.
[02:47] Priya: sure. switching to batch size slider. If we bump concurrency to allow 32 continuous workers and set batching to 8, throughput improves and per-token cost falls further because runtime amortizes kernel overhead. However, batching increases tail latency for individual interactive users.
[03:06] Nora: what's the typical latency hit for an interactive user at batch=8?
[03:10] Priya: depends on arrival distribution. For Eden's current QPS shape we saw median additional latency ~12ms, p95 additional ~60ms at batch=8 with 32 concurrency. That's in the sim.
[03:23] Diego: hmm that p95 is borderline. our SLO is p95 < 350ms.
[03:27] Liam: We can adopt an adaptive policy: route low-latency routes through a smaller-batch pool and background/async routes use higher batch sizes. Console supports route-based optimizer policies and automatic fallback if latency spikes.
[03:41] Samantha: can you map that to dollar numbers?
[03:44] Priya: yes — opening the cost model. Baseline monthly token spend (hosted) $53k. With hybrid-prefetch + batch 8 on background and batch 2 on interactive, simulation shows $23k monthly (roughly 56% savings). If you move to a Dedicated pool with same config plus quantization savings, cost could drop another 18%. But Dedicated has a monthly commit.
[04:12] Diego: can we see the math? I want to compare dedicated commit vs hosted at 1M messages/mo.
[04:18] Priya: I'll export a CSV; attaching the modeled lines. (note: link displayed: https://redwood.app/optimize/cost_model_v3.xlsx). Key rows: baseline tokens/day, tokens served from KV, tokens avoided by prefetch, effective tokens billed to runtime. We also include GPU amortization lines for Dedicated.
[04:40] Nora: I want to understand risk — if our hit rate drops, do we have auto-fallback so users don't see emptiness?
[04:47] Priya: yes, Optimize has TTL policies and a fallback that bypasses the cache and serves directly — also we support multi-tier caching so L1 in-process, L2 managed KV, and L3 persistent prefix store. If hit rate falls, the system will route to the lower-latency pool automatically.
[05:07] Samantha: one of our constraints is that customer data (retrieved docs) cannot persist in a third-party service for more than 30 days. does prefix KV respect TTL and automatic purge?
[05:15] Liam: yes — TTL is configurable and you can enable automatic purge and encryption-at-rest with your KMS. we'll include KMS/HSM options in the security docs we send.
[05:26] Diego: small nit — sometimes our responses include PII from retrieved docs. can we apply redaction pre-cache?
[05:33] Priya: we have pre-cache hooks and you can run a redaction pipeline before writing into KV. that would be in your pipeline; we can show a pattern in the runbook.
[05:43] Samantha: walk me through an end-to-end with a customer session, what gets cached and when.
[05:47] Priya: example: user queries, retriever returns doc A, system builds prompt prefix = system + doc A + recent history. we compute a hash of the static parts (system+doc) and store KV under that key once the model starts generating so subsequent identical prefix hashes hit. lookahead is prefetching likely subsequent tokens for repeated sessions. TTL 12 hours by default in the hybrid profile.
[06:14] Diego: what about session affinity — is that sticky to instance or logical?
[06:18] Priya: logical. session affinity in Redwood is routed at the request layer; you can enable sessionized pools that keep KV cached warm for a user across requests, not tied to a physical instance.
[06:29] Nora: okay good. how do we measure spot regressions — quality regressions when switching model variants / quantization?
[06:35] Liam: Optimize ties into evaluations. we store short eval prompt sets and run canary quality checks comparing outputs (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim). Console flags regressions and can auto-roll back to a fallback model or higher-precision variant.
[06:50] Samantha: excellent. let's talk pilot scope.
[06:53] Priya: propose 2-week pilot: week 1 capture traffic + validate hit rates in sandbox, week 2 run A/B with hybrid-prefetch vs baseline. success criteria: >30% token cost reduction without p95 exceeding current SLO by more than 10%.
[07:09] Diego: we'll need a simple runbook for our infra folks.
[07:13] Liam: we'll send a pilot checklist and a network diagram for the managed vs VPC cache. also SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[07:20] Nora: any gotchas we should be aware of?
[07:23] Priya: watch out for extremely high variability in prompt prefixes — if your retriever returns different passages every call, prefix hit rates collapse and prefetch adds cost. Also be careful with TTL too long — stale cached contexts can cause hallucinations unless you version the prefix keys by doc version.
[07:44] Samantha: noted. can you add a column in the spreadsheet for "retriever stability"?
[07:48] Priya: yes I'll add retriever_stability and show a sensitivity curve.
[07:52] Diego: what's the expected infra work to enable VPC cache?
[07:56] Liam: terraform module, peering, and KMS integration. typically 2-3 infra days + security review. we'll put a template in the handoff.
[08:07] Samantha: can you drop links to the sample configs?
[08:10] Priya: dropped in chat: https://redwood.docs/optimize/runbook and the cost sheet link.
[08:16] Nora: final Q: SLA on Dedicated for p99?
[08:20] Liam: Dedicated customers can get SLA-backed latency targets; p99 depends on instance sizing and autoscale buffers. our standard committed plans include a p99 latency objective, we can surface exact numbers in a follow-up.
[08:32] Samantha: ok let's recap next steps.
[08:34] Liam: recap: we'll send cost_model_v3.xlsx, SOC2/ISO summary, pilot checklist. Priya will provision sandbox. Eden will send anonymized logs and confirm stakeholders. schedule pilot kickoff for week of 12/13.
[08:47] Diego: That works.
[08:49] Nora: thanks everyone.
[08:51] Liam: thanks, we'll follow up.
[58:00] [end of recording]
